title: Frontend: Object.assign()
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Object.assign(). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({target,sources}) for JSON records. Return a shallow own-enumerable key merge with later sources overwriting earlier ones. Skip null sources. Treat __proto__ as an ordinary data key; do not invoke prototype setters.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Convert a non-null target to an object and skip null/undefined sources.
alternativeApproaches: Compare assignment semantics with descriptor copying and immutable object spread without claiming they are identical.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Multiple sources; symbol key; inherited key.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
